headline: Predictive models encoding chromatin and regulatory structure for single-cell data
label: Single Cell Multimodal Prediction Models
summary: Models now embed chromatin, metadata, and cross-modal structure directly into single-cell perturbation, imputation, and integration tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predictive models whose architectures or training objectives encode biological structure, applied mainly to single-cell perturbation response, imputation, and cross-modal linkage. ChromaPert combines paired control RNA and ATAC features to predict cell-state-dependent transcriptional responses, while PIE reformulates response prediction around population-level effects using external knowledge and baseline expression. For unpaired data, scAICT links scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq through adversarial VAE integration with contrastive translation. scCADI conditions diffusion-based imputation on metadata priors, GP-DHT pretrains a dual-head transformer on shared human-mouse genes for GRN link prediction, and GARAGE injects attention-weighted real cell embeddings into a GAN to generate rare-cell-aware data. Chromatin or regulatory information enters the predictive model itself in ChromaPert and scAICT. Bulk, spatial, and therapy-prioritization items address related but distinct questions.
